root_idea.summary: The root centers on the nahr, the upper breast or front of the chest, especially the place reached by a decisive stroke. From this bodily locus developed the verb for stabbing or slaughtering there, with related extensions to facing, adjacency, contest, and mastery.
root_idea.development: The primary physical sense concerns striking or slaughtering at the nahr. Classical usage extends the image to things that face or approach one another, temporal boundaries that meet the next period, people who contend fiercely, and a learned person who has mastered a subject.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The canonical Quranic Form I verb is displayed under the normalized perfect citation form نَحَرَ rather than the attested imperative ٱنْحَرْ.

senses.definition: To slaughter an animal as an offering by nahr—stabbing it at the upper breast or throat.
senses.usage_conditions: In 108:2, the command is understood as an exhortation to perform nahr on a sacrificial offering, paired with prayer. The lexical discussion also records a non-canonical reading in 2:71, فَنَحَرُوهَا, meaning that they slaughtered it.

senses.definition: To place the hands at the neck during the opening takbīr of prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported exegetical interpretation of the command in 108:2; it refers to a prayer gesture rather than animal slaughter.

senses.definition: To subdue desire by metaphorically killing the self.
senses.usage_conditions: Another reported interpretation of 108:2, presenting nahr as disciplined suppression of desire rather than a literal act of slaughter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stab or slaughter a camel or other beast at the nahr; hence, to slay it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary physical verb, especially for striking the animal at the upper breast where the windpipe begins.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or injure a person's nahr, the upper chest or neck-front.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a person as the object of the blow or injury.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To master or know affairs, knowledge, or poetry thoroughly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which thorough intellectual command is expressed as mastering the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perform or recite the prayer at the first part of its appointed time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative conventional use referring specifically to prayer performed early.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression نَحَرَهُمُ اللهُ, to hasten to do them good; alternatively, to slay them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported expression with two transmitted interpretations; the slaying interpretation overlaps the literal branch, while the hastening interpretation is idiomatic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To face, front, or stand opposite someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person facing another person, or of houses or dwellings facing one another or a road.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The uppermost breast, chest, or bosom, especially the place of the collar or necklace; also the point at which an animal is stabbed for slaughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The anatomical noun may denote the chest generally or the more specific slaughtering point where the windpipe begins.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first part or commencement of the day, month, or midday period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal extension of the notion of an upper or foremost part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The position directly in front of, facing, or opposite another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing one person or thing as situated before or opposite another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stab or slay one another in combat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI use referring to mutual violence at the nahr.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend mutually and greedily for something, as though nearly killing one another over it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative reciprocal construction for extreme avarice, tenacity, or rivalry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To face or front one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI use applied especially to houses or places of abode.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stab oneself at the nahr, and hence to kill oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive Form VIII use; in a proverb it may instead mean to bring about one's own destruction figuratively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cloud, to burst with abundant water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to a cloud releasing a great quantity of rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In open view; openly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional adverbial expression, as in لَقِيتُهُ صَحْرَةً بَحْرَةً نَحْرَةً.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A learned, skilled, intelligent, and experienced person; an expert.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes someone thoroughly versed in what he does, figuratively connected with mastering knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal stabbed at the manḥar; slaughtered. Figuratively, a son devoted to be sacrificed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective or noun may describe the slaughtered animal itself or, figuratively, one dedicated for sacrifice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A temporal boundary of the month, especially its first day or, according to another usage, its last day or last night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The authorities differ over whether the term denotes the beginning or the end of the month; it can also include the last night together with the following day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A facing or opposite part; something situated in front of another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested especially in the plural expression نَوَاحِرُ الأَرْضِ for parts facing or opposite the land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intensive epithet for a great slaughterer of camels; figuratively, liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative generosity is associated with lavish slaughtering of valuable camels for guests or recipients.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Faced or fronted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial use derived from the notion of being directly opposite something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two veins in a horse's chest; the dāʾirat al-nāḥir is an anatomical mark in the throat region below them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized anatomical terminology recorded in the root's classical lexical discussion.

cautions: The QAC occurrence is the imperative ٱنْحَرْ; the public headword is normalized to the Form I perfect citation form نَحَرَ.
The sacrifice reading of 108:2 is presented as the principal Quranic lexical sense, while the hand-position and desire-suppression readings are reported interpretive alternatives.
The reading فَنَحَرُوهَا associated with 2:71 is explicitly identified as non-canonical in the supplied lexical evidence and is not counted as a QAC occurrence.
